newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON COASTS AFTER SLEEPING WITH HOTEL LIGHTS ON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON COASTS AFTER SLEEPING WITH HOTEL LIGHTS ON.

text.p: Defending world champion Allen Johnson coasted through the opening round of the men's 110 metres hurdles on Tuesday after sleeping all night with the light on in his hotel room to ensure he got up in time.

Johnson, seeking to retain his world title after winning the Olympic crown in Atlanta, clocked a comfortable 13.52 seconds, making no effort to catch heat winner, Dan Philibert of France who won the race in 13.43 seconds.
Afterwards Johnson said he had slept all night with the light on in his hotel room because he was so afraid of over-sleeping and missing the 9.15 a.m. race start.
"I've been up since 4.30 this morning, I was scared I would oversleep so I slept with the lights on and my watch on," said Johnson, a notorious late-sleeper.
He added that whoever won the final would probably break the world record of 12.91 seconds set by Britain's Colin Jackson when he won the title at the 1993 Stuttgart championships.
"I hope it's me, I'm in the shape to do it," said the American.

Jackson, with something to prove after injury forced him to concede his world title to Johnson in 1995 and lack of form deprived him of an Olympic medal in Atlanta, looked impressive in his heat, winning in 13.19 seconds, the fastest time of the round.

Medal contenders Mark Crear of the United States (13.46), Igor Kovac of Slovakia (13.36), Florian Schwarthoff of Germany (13.44), Tony Jarrett of Britain (13.35) and Anier Garcia of Cuba (13.46) all qualified for the second round later on Tuesday.
But there was disappointment for Cuba's Olympic finalist Emilio Valle, who went out in the opening round after pulling up after the third hurdle with a thigh injury.

There were no surprises in the first round of the women's 400 hurdles with Olympic champion Deon Hemmings of the United States (54.42) and her compatriot Kim Batten (54.46) , the defending champion and world record holder, both qualifying easily.
